name: Chinese modern woodcut
summary: In 1931 Lu Xun urged young artists to learn the European expressionist woodcut of Kollwitz and Masereel. They cut black-and-white prints on cheap wood and printed many on thin paper, bold and rough.

philosophy.core_thesis: A cheap block of wood and one knife can give a poor and angry public a picture of its own life and its own fight.
design_principles: Cut the block yourself, with a knife, in black ink on white, or in black and one flat colour.
Build the image from heavy black masses and white knife lines, and keep the contrast high.
Choose the people as the subject: workers, farmers, soldiers, a crowd, a portrait of a hero.
Cut the line rough and angular, 0.5–2 mm wide. Leave the knife edge visible.
Allow some cross-cut hatching in the shadow, but keep most tones as a mass or a white line.
Print many copies on thin paper by hand rubbing with a spoon or a baren, so the print is cheap to share.
Add a short caption or a date, and keep the sheet small enough for a magazine page or a wall.
anti_patterns: A soft colour gradient or a pastel set
A clean vector edge with no cut mark
A pretty or neutral subject with no social point

process.matrix: A plank of pear or boxwood, cut on the face with a knife.
process.press: No press. The artist rubs the back of the thin sheet with a spoon or a baren.
process.image_making: The artist draws, cuts and prints. Study groups and schools teach the craft.
process.edition: Hundreds to thousands of cheap copies.

inks.strategy: One black ink, sometimes with one flat colour added from a second block. Print on thin paper.

screening.rule: Make a tone with heavy black masses and white knife lines, with some cross-cut hatching at about 30 lines an inch.

registration.rule: One block prints all the image, so there is no register. A second block for colour can shift 1–2 mm.

substrate.stock: Thin Chinese paper of bamboo or bark fibre.
substrate.finish: Unsized and absorbent, with a soft, thin sheet.

surface.impression: Light. The ink shows a slight emboss on the back of the thin sheet.
surface.sheen: Matt black ink on matt paper.
surface.texture: Dense black masses, rough knife edges, and the fibres of thin paper.

marks: portrait of a hero or a worker

emotion.target_response: Urgency and solidarity: the viewer feels a hard truth cut in black, and a people who stand together.

use_cases: posters and covers on social themes
editorial images on history and labour
avoid_when: The brief needs soft colour or a decorative mood.
The picture needs a photographic tone.

modifiers.how: Add 3–5 flat colour blocks in vermilion, green and yellow, and fill the sheet with auspicious motifs.
Cut deeper gouge marks, show the plank grain, and print on a heavy cream paper.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Lu Xun Academy of Fine Arts
